claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me: **How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm inquiring about my child Alex. Just the one.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'm now going to ask you some questions to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**First, could you tell me: Is Alex under 16 years old, or is Alex aged 16-19 and in approved education or training (such as A-levels, vocational training, or an apprenticeship)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex is actually 21 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know that Alex is 21 years old.

I'm afraid this means that Alex does not meet the age requirements for Child Benefit. Child Benefit is only available for children who are:
- Under 16 years old, or
- Aged 16-19 and in approved full-time education or training

Since Alex is 21 years old and therefore falls outside these age criteria, you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Is there anything else I can help you with, or do you have any other children you'd like me to assess?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Wait, but Alex receives Universal Credit in their own name. Doesn't that make a difference?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a good question. However, the fact that Alex receives Universal Credit in their own name doesn't change the Child Benefit eligibility rules. 

Child Benefit eligibility is based on the child's age and their education/training status, not on what other benefits they may be receiving. Since Alex is 21 years old, they fall outside the eligible age range for Child Benefit, regardless of any other benefits they might be claiming.

The rules are:
- Child Benefit is for children under 16, or
- Aged 16-19 in approved full-time education or training

At 21, Alex doesn't meet either of these criteria.

Do you have any other children you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, that's it. Just Alex. I guess I misunderstood the rules then. Thanks for clarifying.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're welcome! It's an easy misunderstanding to make – the rules around benefits can be quite complex. I'm glad I could clarify things for you.

Now let me confirm the outcome based on our conversation:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: If you have any other questions about benefits in the future, feel free to ask. Best of luck!
